86:1: Interpretation of Surat At-Tariq Abdullah bin Imam Ahmad said: My father told us, Abdullah bin Muhammad told us, Abdullah said, and I heard it from him, Marwan bin Muawiyah Al-Fazari told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abdul Rahman Al-Ta’ifi, on the authority of Abdul Rahman bin Khalid bin Abi Jabal Al-Adwani, on the authority of his father that he saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the east of Thaqif, standing on a bow or a staff when he came to them seeking victory from them, and I heard him say: By the sky and the nightcomer, until he finished it. He said: So I memorized it in the pre-Islamic period while I was a polytheist, then I recited it in Islam. He said: Thaqif called me and said: What did you hear from this man? So I recited it to them, and those who were with them from Quraysh said, “We know our companion best. If we knew what he was saying was true, we would have followed him.” An-Nasa’i said: Amr ibn Mansur told us, Abu Nu’aym told us, on the authority of Mis’ar, on the authority of Muharrib ibn Dithar, on the authority of Jabir, who said, “Mu’adh prayed the Maghrib prayer and recited Al-Baqarah and An-Nisa’. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘You are a temptress, O Mu’adh! Was it not sufficient for you to recite By the sky and At-Tariq and Ash-Shams and its brightness and the like?’” In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful God the Blessed and Exalted swears by the heaven and what He has placed in it of luminous stars. For this reason He the Most High said: By the heaven and the Nightcomer. Then He said: And what can make you know what is the Nightcomer? Then He explained it by saying: the piercing star. Qatada and others said: The star is called a piercing star because it is only seen at night and disappears during the day. This is supported by what came in the authentic hadith in which he forbade a man from knocking on the door of his family, meaning that he should come to them suddenly at night. And in another hadith which includes the supplication: Except a nightcomer who knocks with good, O Most Merciful. And the statement of God the Most High: the piercing star. Ibn Abbas said: It means: the shining star. Al-Suddi said: It pierces the devils when it is sent upon them. Ikrimah said: It is shining and burns the devils. God the Almighty says: Indeed, every soul has a protector over it. That is, every soul has a protector from God who guards it from harm, as God the Almighty says: He has guardian angels before him and behind him who guard him by the command of God. And His saying: So let man consider from what he was created. This is a warning to man about the weakness of the origin from which he was created and a guidance for him to acknowledge the Resurrection, because He who was able to begin is even more able to repeat, as God the Almighty says: And it is He who begins creation and then repeats it, and that is easier for Him. And His saying: He created from a fluid ejected means semen that flows out of the man and the woman, and a child is born from them, by God’s permission. That is why He said: It emerges from between the backbone and the ribs meaning the backbone of the man and the ribs of the woman, which is her chest. Shabib bin Bishr said on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas, It emerges from between the backbone and the ribs. The backbone of the man and the ribs of the woman are yellow and thin, and the child can only be from them. This is what Saeed bin Jubair, Ikrimah, Qatadah, Al-Suddi and others said. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Saeed Al-Ashj told us, Abu Usamah told us on the authority of Misa’ar, I heard Al-Hakam mention on the authority of Ibn Abbas, It emerges from between the backbone and the ribs. He said: These are the ribs, and he placed his hand on his chest. Ad-Dahhak and Atiyah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The rib of a woman is the place of the necklace. Ikrimah and Saeed bin Jubair said the same. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The ribs are between her breasts. Mujahid said: The ribs are between the shoulders to the chest. He also said: The ribs are lower than the collarbones. Sufyan Ath-Thawri said: Above the breasts. Saeed bin Jubair said: The ribs are four ribs on this lower side. Ad-Dahhak said: The ribs are between the breasts, legs, and eyes. Al-Layth bin Saad said on the authority of Muammar bin Abi Habeeba Al-Madani that he heard regarding the statement of God, the Almighty: It emerges from between the backbone and the ribs, he said: It is the juice of the heart, from there the child is born. Qatada said: It emerges from between the backbone and the ribs from between his backbone and his throat. And the Almighty’s saying: Indeed, He is Able to return it. There are two opinions about it. One of them is that He is Able to return this gushing water to the place from which it emerged. This was stated by Mujahid, Ikrimah, and others. The second opinion is that He is able to return this human being who was created from gushing water, that is, to bring him back and resurrect him to the Hereafter, because He who has the power to begin is also able to bring him back. God Almighty has mentioned this proof in the Qur’an in more than one place, and this opinion was said by Ad-Dahhak and chosen by Ibn Jarir. For this reason, God Almighty said: The Day when secrets will be exposed, meaning on the Day of Resurrection, secrets will be exposed, meaning they will be revealed and become apparent, and the secret will remain public and the hidden will be famous. It has been proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Ibn Umar that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “A banner will be raised for every traitor at his backside, and it will be said: This is the treachery of so-and-so, son of so-and-so.” And God Almighty said: Then he will have, meaning man on the Day of Resurrection, no strength, meaning in himself, nor helper, meaning outside of him, meaning he will not be able to save himself from God’s punishment, and no one will be able to do that for him.

That is why He said: It emerges from between the backbone and the ribs meaning the backbone of the man and the ribs of the woman, which is her chest. Shabib bin Bishr said on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas, It emerges from between the backbone and the ribs. The backbone of the man and the ribs of the woman are yellow and thin, and the child can only be from them. This is what Saeed bin Jubair, Ikrimah, Qatadah, Al-Suddi and others said. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Saeed Al-Ashj told us, Abu Usamah told us on the authority of Misa’ar, I heard Al-Hakam mention on the authority of Ibn Abbas, It emerges from between the backbone and the ribs. He said: These are the ribs, and he placed his hand on his chest. Ad-Dahhak and Atiyah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The rib of a woman is the place of the necklace. Ikrimah and Saeed bin Jubair said the same. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The ribs are between her breasts. Mujahid said: The ribs are between the shoulders to the chest. He also said: The ribs are lower than the collarbones. Sufyan Ath-Thawri said: Above the breasts. Saeed bin Jubair said: The ribs are four ribs on this lower side. Ad-Dahhak said: The ribs are between the breasts, legs, and eyes. 86:11: Ibn Abbas said: The return is the rain, and from him: It is the clouds in which there is rain, and from him: And the sky with its returns It rains and then rains, and Qatada said: The sustenance of the servants returns every year and were it not for that they and their livestock would perish, and Ibn Zayd said: Its stars return and its sun and moon come from here And the earth with its cracks Ibn Abbas said: It is its cracking to produce plants, and this is what Saeed bin Jubair, Ikrimah, Abu Malik, Ad-Dahhak, Al-Hasan, Qatada, As-Suddi and others said. And the Almighty said: Indeed, it is a decisive statement. Ibn Abbas said: It is true, and Qatadah said the same. Another said: It is a just judgment. And it is not a joke. That is, it is the truth. Then He informed about the disbelievers that they deny it and turn people away from His path, saying: Indeed, they are plotting a plot. That is, they are plotting against the people by calling them to something that is contrary to the Qur’an. Then the Almighty said: So give the disbelievers respite. That is, give them respite and do not be impatient for them. Give them respite for a while. That is, a little, and you will see what torment, humiliation, punishment, and destruction He will bring upon them, as the Almighty said: We will give them enjoyment for a little; then We will force them to a severe punishment. The end of the interpretation of Surat At-Tariq. And praise and thanks be to God.
